item.title: ROUNDUP: Vueve’s double-double buoys Sierra in boys hoops win over Franklin
item.description: Sierra’s boys basketball team rolled to its fifth straight win Wednesday, getting a double-double from Colby Vueve while holding off visiting Franklin, 57-42.

item.title: Knights shut out Ripon in TVL boys soccer opener
item.description: The Ripon Christian Knights capitalized on great defensive play and strong finishing around the net Wednesday night in a 3-0 shutout victory over the Ripon Indians in the Trans Valley League opener for both squads.

item.title: Indians handle RC behind Hendryx’s 1st-half hat trick
item.description: Barely three minutes into the match Wednesday night Mia Hendryx notched the first of her three first-half goals for host Ripon on the way to a 6-0 Trans-Valley League girls soccer opener against Ripon Christian at Stouffer Field.

item.title: Lathrop locks down Sierra, improves to 11-0
item.description: Lathrop remains undefeated through 11 games, and the Spartans are doing it with defense. On Wednesday, they continued their best start in program history with a comfortable 50-34 triumph over visiting Sierra.

item.title: Zipping over Altamont at 125 mph: But first get ready to hop aboard ACE in downtown Manteca
item.description: The rail project that, by extremely wide margins, will move more people and reduce more greenhouse gases per dollar invested is likely to be up and running by 2027. No, it’s not the much-ballyhooed California High Speed Rail which, with apologies to Zager & Evans, will be completed in 2525 if man is still alive.

item.title: Ripon Unified board continues with same trustees as officers
item.description: The same officers of the Ripon Unified School District will remain intact for another year.

item.title: TERRACES AT BETHANY
item.description: The Terraces at Bethany was a long time in the making.

item.title: SJ Valley lags in use of zero-emission vehicles
item.description: The eight counties in the San Joaquin Valley experience some of the highest levels of air pollution in California, with levels of several pollutants far above the statewide average.

item.title: $18.5M navigation center will house 190 homeless plus 8 transitional units
item.description: An industrial building that once was part of the Kodak photo processing network will house 190 homeless as Manteca’s permanent navigation center. The cost and extent of the project at 555 Industrial Park Drive was outlined in an environmental assessment required by the federal Housing and Urban Development completed last month.

item.title: WALKABLE NEIGHBORHOODS WITH 100% RENTALS AT RIVER ISLANDS
item.description: River Islands at Lathrop could be targeting a new housing market for the Northern San Joaquin Valley. And in doing so, it could end up building 2,000 homes in as little as two years.
